fields.Front: How is an entity drawn in Crow's Foot notation?
fields.Back: A box with the entity name in a header and the attributes listed inside (key marked), instead of a rectangle with attribute ovals.

fields.Front: How is a relationship drawn in Crow's Foot notation?
fields.Back: With just a line between the entities (no diamond); the end of the line shows both the cardinality and the participation.

fields.Front: Crow's Foot: what are the four possible line ends?
fields.Back: Zero or more (circle + crow's foot); one or more (bar + crow's foot); one and only one (bar + bar); zero or one (circle + bar).

fields.Text: Crow's Foot line ends: circle + crow's foot = {{c1::zero or more}}; bar + crow's foot = {{c2::one or more}}; bar + bar = {{c3::one and only one}}; circle + bar = {{c4::zero or one}}.

fields.Front: In a Crow's Foot line end, which mark gives the maximum and which the minimum?
fields.Back: The outer mark (touching the entity) gives the maximum: bar = 1, crow's foot = many. The inner mark gives the minimum: circle = 0 (partial), bar = 1 (total).

fields.Text: In Crow's Foot notation the three-pronged symbol means {{c1::many}} and the circle means {{c2::optional (minimum zero)}}.

fields.Front: Translate A ||-------o< B (Crow's Foot) into Chen cardinality and participation.
fields.Back: 1:N from A to B; B total (each B has exactly one A), A partial (an A has zero or more Bs); (1,1) beside B, (0,N) beside A.

fields.Front: DVD store example: what is the Crow's Foot line for CUSTOMER 'currently renting' DVDCOPY?
fields.Back: CUSTOMER end: zero or one (a copy is rented by at most one customer); DVDCOPY end: zero or more (a customer may be renting none or many). Customers may never have rented.

fields.Front: DVD store example: what is the Crow's Foot line for DVDCOPY 'is a' MOVIE?
fields.Back: MOVIE end: one and only one (each copy is a copy of exactly one movie; no blank DVDs, no two movies on one disc). DVDCOPY end: one or more (the store only keeps track of a movie if it has at least one copy; a popular movie has many).

fields.Front: DVD store example: list the three entities and their attributes.
fields.Back: CUSTOMER (CustomerID, FirstName, LastName); MOVIE (MovieID, Title, Year); DVDCOPY (DVDID, HomeStore).

fields.Front: Which notation does the course use, and why does the instructor teach Crow's Foot anyway?
fields.Back: Chen notation (rectangles and ovals, 'the standard notation people usually use'); Crow's Foot so you recognise it elsewhere. It looks closer to UML diagrams.

fields.Text: Slide example: a student fills {{c1::one and only one}} seat and every seat is filled by a student: one-to-one with {{c2::total}} participation on both sides.

fields.Front: Instructor teaches Course (Crow's Foot slide): read both ends.
fields.Back: An instructor teaches one or many courses (must teach at least one); a course is taught by one and only one instructor.

fields.Text: Professor teaches Section: a professor teaches {{c1::zero or many}} sections (they might be doing research); a section is taught by {{c2::one and only one}} professor.

fields.Front: Planets example: read the four line ends.
fields.Back: A planet circles zero or one star (an asteroid circles none); a star has zero or many planets; a planet has zero or many moons; a moon orbits at least one planet.

fields.Text: DVD store: DVDCOPY is separate from MOVIE because there may be {{c1::five copies of Star Wars}}; a customer rents a {{c2::DVD}}, not a movie.

fields.Front: draw.io demo: what line did the instructor choose for CUSTOMER currently renting CAR, and why?
fields.Back: Optional one to optional one: a customer might not be renting and rents at most one car at a time; a car might not be rented and is rented by at most one customer.

fields.Text: In Crow's Foot the mark closer to the {{c1::entity}} is the maximum (cardinality) and the mark closer to the {{c2::middle of the line}} is the participation.
